analysis.investment_thesis: Campus Activewear has genuine brand strength in India's mass-premium footwear segment with impressive ROE (29.5%) and ROCE (31.8%), but at 55.7x trailing P/E the price demands growth that the business hasn't delivered — revenue has essentially stagnated at ₹1,448–1,593 Cr over three years. I don't pay wonderful prices for merely good businesses, and the earnings volatility here disqualifies it entirely at current levels.
key_strengths: High returns on capital: ROE 29.5%, ROCE 31.8% — genuinely excellent for a consumer brand
Gross margin of 52% suggests real pricing power in its mass-premium niche; OCF positive all 5 years
Strong promoter conviction at 72% holding and meaningful debt reduction (₹335 Cr → ₹232 Cr)
key_risks: Earnings chronically volatile and margin-compressed: operating income peaked at ₹242 Cr (FY22) and is still only ₹183 Cr in FY25 — three years of no earnings progress
Valuation is punishing: 55.7x P/E and 33x EV/EBITDA price in perfection while revenue grew only 10% in two years (₹1,448 → ₹1,593 Cr)
Weak competitive moat — squeezed between global brands (Nike, Adidas) above and commodity players below, with no durable pricing fortress
red_flags: Operating income regression: ₹242 Cr (FY22) → ₹143 Cr (FY24) — margin structurally compressed despite revenue scale-up
Net profit of ₹121 Cr on ₹7,573 Cr market cap implies ~62x real earnings multiple with zero growth tailwind
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Campus Activewear is a decent business masquerading at a great-business valuation. The ROE of 29.5% and ROCE of 31.8% catch the eye, and a 52% gross margin suggests the Campus brand carries real weight in India's mass-premium sports footwear segment. Free cash flow has genuinely improved — ₹219 Cr in FY24 and ₹176 Cr in FY25 — and the promoter's 72% stake signals owner mentality. But wonderful returns on equity only stay wonderful if the business can deploy incremental capital at similar rates, and the recent evidence doesn't inspire confidence.

The numbers that trouble me most: operating income peaked at ₹242 Cr in FY22 and still hasn't surpassed that three years later (₹183 Cr in FY25). Net profit is back to ₹121 Cr but only modestly above FY23's ₹117 Cr — no compounding in sight. Revenue grew just 10% across FY23–FY25 combined. Yet the market prices this at 55.7x trailing earnings and 33x EV/EBITDA. That's a price that demands a wonderful business with a durable moat, and Campus — facing global athletic giants above and price warriors below — simply doesn't have one. D/E of 0.48 is tolerable but above my comfort zone. I'd want to pay no more than 25–30x earnings for a business of this quality, implying a price closer to ₹120–145. At ₹248, I'll cheerfully watch from the sidelines.
